extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale, and a contamination-free benchmark for agentic software engineering.
extraction.license: Permissive licenses (e.g., MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-4-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, ISC, CC0-1.0, ZPL-2.1, Other manually verified permissive licenses)
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: An automated pipeline for mining real-world software engineering tasks from GitHub, covering environment configuration, build setup, and test validation. The pipeline comprises four stages: preliminary task collection, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and quality assessment.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Primary sources are GitHub Archive and GitHub. Approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025, from over 30,000 repositories with permissive licenses and Python constituting over 75% of the codebase lines of code.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For each selected pull request, the overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch, containing changes to non-test files intended to address the issue, and a test patch, comprising only changes to test files.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filtering criteria applied: issue from a Python repository with a permissive license, issue marked as resolved, PR merged into main branch, PR not linked to multiple issues, issue description longer than 10 characters, PR introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files, changes affect 1 to 15 files. After filtering, approximately 153,400 potential task instances remain.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated task quality assessment using an instruction-following model fine-tuned on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness. The model receives the issue description, the canonical solution patch, and the test patch as input and predicts binary quality labels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy for Task Complexity, 67% accuracy for Test Patch Correctness, and 79% accuracy for Issue Clarity on a validation set. LLM-generated labels are provided as metadata with each task instance to allow filtering.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Three labels per task instance: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, Test Patch Correctness
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face Datasets. The benchmark leaderboard is continuously updated with fresh tasks to ensure decontamination. The pipeline enables continuous collection and processing of tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark may accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, bringing potential risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. Fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concerns.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems. The automated pipeline may result in some tasks being imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue, leading to lower absolute success rates compared to manually curated benchmarks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automated task quality assessment may contain errors and cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment. Limited language diversity (Python only). Some tasks may be imperfectly described or unsolvable solely from the issue. The pipeline relies on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning for reinforcement learning of SWE agents at scale. The dataset is designed for interactive agent training and robust benchmarking. Usage guidelines include filtering tasks based on LLM-generated quality labels for task difficulty control.
